# Specification: Dependency updates

## 1. Business Goal

<!-- last written by: spec-author, 2026-10-08 -->

Every version this repository depends on - packages, the SDK, local tools, workflow actions - is pinned, so without a mechanism they age silently until an update is large and urgent at once; and the one mechanism that would update them indiscriminately would also move the engine's three dependencies off the baseline dependency versions before the baseline exists, breaking the extraction the whole of epic `0001` is measured against. This Feature removes that failure state: Renovate proposes updates as pull requests grouped by ecosystem, a minor or patch update merges itself once every required check passes, a major waits for a person, and the engine's dependencies are left alone until `0001-F1`'s golden baseline test exists (its B-004).

## 2. User Needs

<!-- last written by: spec-author, 2026-10-09 -->

| #   | Persona        | Need                                                                                        | Pain Point Today                            |
| --- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | The maintainer | Routine updates applied without attention, and only when the build agrees                   | Every update is a manual edit               |
| 2   | The maintainer | A breaking update shown to a person before it lands                                         | Nothing distinguishes a major from a patch  |
| 3   | The reviewer   | One pull request per ecosystem, not one per package                                         | The configuration present groups NuGet only |
| 4   | `0001-F1`      | The engine's three dependencies held at the baseline dependency versions until the baseline | Nothing excludes them                       |

### Assumptions

| ID  | Assumption                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A-1 | The schedule and timezone in `.github/renovate.json` today (before 6am on Monday, America/Chicago) are kept; the owner did not change them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| A-2 | Renovate runs self-hosted, as a scheduled workflow in this repository using `renovatebot/github-action`, and a merge without a person relies on the repository allowing it (`0055-F8`). Amended 2026-10-08 by OQ-6; it assumed the hosted app before. Amended 2026-10-09 by decision 0001: "self-hosted" means a self-hosted Renovate, not a self-hosted runner; the job runs on GitHub's hosted `ubuntu-latest` runner, where `renovatebot/github-action` runs the Renovate container, and uses no infrastructure of the owner's. |
| A-3 | "The engine's three dependencies" are Markdig, YamlDotNet and JsonSchema.Net, the `Engine` group of `Directory.Packages.props` (`0001-F1` C-7).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

## 4. Constraints

<!-- last written by: spec-author, 2026-10-09, 2026-10-28 (0075) -->

| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| C-1 | The engine's three dependencies are excluded from updates until `0001-F1` B-004's golden baseline test is on `main`; the exclusion is lifted by a change made after that test lands that cites it and that also amends `0001-F1` C-7, which pins the baseline dependency versions with no end - a cross-Feature dependency on `0001-F1`.                                                                                                                                                                | Lifting the exclusion before that test lands; lifting it while `0001-F1` C-7 still pins the versions; an update that moves the engine off the baseline dependency versions before the golden report is committed (`0001-F1` B-004). |
| C-2 | Renovate's behaviour is the configuration checked in to this repository, including the self-hosted run's own settings.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | A setting passed to the run only on a command line, in an uncommitted environment value or in a web interface, which no pull request reviews.                                                                                       |
| C-3 | An update never edits a generated workflow file by hand; a generated workflow changes in an update pull request only as the build's regeneration output (amended 2026-10-08, OQ-5).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | A Renovate rule matching a file under `.github/workflows/`; a regex or manual edit of a generated workflow (`0055-F2` C-1).                                                                                                         |
| C-4 | A version is changed only where it is declared once: `Directory.Packages.props`, `global.json` or the local tool manifest.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | A version written into a `.csproj` to satisfy an update.                                                                                                                                                                            |

## 7. Technical Design

<!-- last written by: implementer, 2026-10-09, 2026-10-28 (0075) -->

Delivered so far by items 0073, 0074 and 0075; 0075 is under "Action versions and the post-upgrade regeneration (0075)" below. The merge policy (0076) and reading the feed (0077) are not built yet.

- **The declaration** is [`.build/SpechtBuild.Renovate.cs`](../../.build/SpechtBuild.Renovate.cs): a second Rocket.Surgery.Nuke `[GitHubActionsSteps]` beside `ci`, named `renovate`, on `ubuntu-latest`, writing [`.github/workflows/renovate.yml`](../workflows/renovate.yml) with `AutoGenerate` on, so any build run regenerates it and the regeneration is committed with the build change (C-8, `0055-F2` C-1). `InvokedTargets` is empty, so the generator emits no `--target` step. Its `RenovateMiddleware` enhancement shapes the rest; the generator keeps the configuration object it passed in, so the middleware changes it in place. The job keeps the generator's name, `build`.
- **The schedule** (B-015) is `OnCronSchedule = "0 10 * * 1"`: 10:00 UTC on Monday, which is 5am CDT and 4am CST, inside Renovate's own `before 6am on monday` window in America/Chicago (A-1). Renovate's `schedule` in [`.github/renovate.json`](../renovate.json) still decides when a branch is created; the cron only starts the run. `RENOVATE_REPOSITORIES: ${{ github.repository }}` points the run at this repository and nothing else.
- **The manual trigger** (decision 0001, § 5 row 6) is a detailed `workflow_dispatch` trigger the middleware adds to `DetailedTriggers`. The attribute's `On` is not used: setting it switches the generator to short triggers and drops the schedule.
- **The job's steps** are replaced wholesale by the middleware, which also drops the generator's `dotnet tool restore` and global NUKE install; the run needs neither. They are `actions/checkout@v4`; a bash step that writes `DOTNET_SDK_VERSION=$(jq -r .sdk.version global.json)` to `$GITHUB_ENV`; and `renovatebot/github-action@v46.3.7`, whose default `renovate-version` at that tag is `44`. The SDK version is read from `global.json` when the run starts, never baked into the workflow at generation, so an SDK update (B-003) needs no regeneration.
- **The credential** (C-8, decision 0001) is `token: ${{ secrets.RENOVATE_TOKEN }}`, so the pull requests Renovate opens start the workflow runs they wait on. The workflow's own token is cut to `contents: read` and nothing else; B-017's `packages: read` is 0077's.
- **The SDK before any post-upgrade task** (B-016). The action runs Renovate as the `ghcr.io/renovatebot/renovate` container on the hosted runner, where Docker is preinstalled (decision 0001), so an SDK set up on the runner would not reach a post-upgrade task inside the container. The action instead starts the container as `root` (`docker-user`) with [`.github/renovate-entrypoint.sh`](../renovate-entrypoint.sh) as its command (`docker-cmd-file`) and passes `DOTNET_SDK_VERSION` in (`additional-env-list`). The script runs containerbase's `install-tool dotnet "$DOTNET_SDK_VERSION"`, then `runuser -u ubuntu renovate` - the action's documented pattern for this - so the SDK `global.json` pins is installed before Renovate starts, and therefore before any post-upgrade task.
- **The self-hosted run's settings** (C-2) are committed in [`.github/renovate-global.json`](../renovate-global.json), passed as `configurationFile`: `platform: github`, `onboarding: false` and `requireConfig: required`, so the run reads this repository's `.github/renovate.json` and opens no onboarding pull request. 0075 adds `allowedCommands` and `customEnvVariables` (C-7, B-018; below).
- **No issue** (B-010, C-5): `.github/renovate.json` sets `dependencyDashboard: false`. The NuGet major rule whose only setting was `dependencyDashboardApproval` is removed, because that approval lives in the dashboard issue C-5 forbids; a major waiting as an open pull request is 0076's B-007. **The label** (B-011) is the existing `labels: ["dependencies"]`, kept.
- **The rules** are the `packageRules` in [`.github/renovate.json`](../renovate.json), delivered by 0074. Renovate applies every rule that matches an update in order, and a later rule's setting wins, so the order is part of the design: the three grouping rules first, then the C-4 hold, then the engine hold last, so nothing after it can switch an engine dependency back on. Each rule carries a `description` citing the id it serves. They replace 0073's single rule, which put every NuGet minor and patch update, the SDK and the local tools included, into one group.
- **NuGet packages** (B-001): the `nuget` manager, `matchFileNames: ["Directory.Packages.props"]`, minor and patch, `groupName: "NuGet packages"`, branch `renovate/nuget-packages`. **Local tools** (B-004): the same manager and update types with `matchFileNames: [".config/dotnet-tools.json"]`, `groupName: "dotnet local tools"`, branch `renovate/dotnet-local-tools`. Renovate gives a package in either file the same `depType`, `nuget`, so the file name is the only thing that tells the two groups apart. **The .NET SDK** (B-003) is keyed instead by `matchDepTypes: ["dotnet-sdk"]`, the type the `nuget` manager gives `global.json`'s `sdk.version`, `groupName: ".NET SDK"`, branch `renovate/net-sdk`.
- **The C-4 hold**: a `nuget` rule whose `matchFileNames` lists only negations - `!Directory.Packages.props`, `!global.json`, `!.config/dotnet-tools.json` - with `enabled: false`. In Renovate 44 a list of negations alone matches every file none of them names, so a version declared anywhere else, a `Version` written into a `.csproj` included, is never updated. Today no file outside those three declares a version: the `.csproj` and `Directory.Build.props` references carry none, and Renovate already skips them as `invalid-version`.
- **The engine hold** (B-008, C-1): `matchPackageNames: ["Markdig", "YamlDotNet", "JsonSchema.Net"]` with `enabled: false`, last, so a major, a minor and a patch alike are never proposed and no later rule can re-enable them. Its `description` records the lift condition: a change made after `0001-F1` B-004's golden baseline test is on `main`, citing it, that also amends `0001-F1` C-7. TestableIO.System.IO.Abstractions sits in the same `Engine` item group in `Directory.Packages.props` but is not one of the three baseline dependency pins, so it groups with the other packages.
- **Interim state until the token exists.** With 0074 the engine's three dependencies are held (B-008, C-1), and with 0075 the `github-actions` manager is disabled, so no manager reads a file under `.github/workflows/` (C-3). Until the owner creates the `RENOVATE_TOKEN` secret, every scheduled and manual run fails red at the Renovate step: `renovatebot/github-action@v46.3.7` (`src/input.ts`) throws when its `token` input is empty, so Renovate never starts and the run opens nothing. Before 0075 lands, creating the secret would let a run propose exactly what C-3 rules out; item 0091, whose checklist has the owner create it, waits on 0075 for that reason.
- **An SDK update branch for 0075** (B-003, B-016). The run reads `DOTNET_SDK_VERSION` from the default branch's `global.json`, so it installs the SDK `main` pins. On a branch that raises that pin, `rollForward: latestFeature` rolls only forward from the requested version, never back to the older SDK installed, so a build on that branch cannot start. 0075's post-upgrade workflow generation must therefore not run on SDK updates. This is a handoff to 0075, not a claim; `renovate.yml` itself needs no regeneration for an SDK update (the job's steps above). 0075's design keeps it: no rule carrying the post-upgrade task matches the SDK (below).
- **Verified** when 0073 was delivered: `./build.sh Compile` regenerated `renovate.yml` alone, leaving `ci.yml` unchanged; `renovate-config-validator --strict` at Renovate 44 accepted both JSON files; `Format` and `Test` passed. No run has been observed on GitHub yet, and nothing here has a test (§ 8).
- **Verified** when 0074 was delivered, locally and not on GitHub: `renovate-config-validator --strict` at Renovate 44.149.0 accepted both JSON files, as global and as repository configuration. A `--platform=local --dry-run=lookup` run of Renovate 44 against this tree, with no token, returned 3 branches: `renovate/nuget-packages` (xunit.v3 4.0.1 to 4.0.2, Rocket.Surgery.Airframe.CodeAnalysis 0.12.1 to 0.12.2), `renovate/net-sdk` (`global.json`'s `dotnet-sdk`, `depType` `dotnet-sdk`, 10.0.100 to 10.0.401) and `renovate/major-dotnet-monorepo` (System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 9.0.20 to 10.0.12, a major grouped by `config:recommended`'s monorepo preset, which is 0076's to settle under B-007 and B-012). Markdig, YamlDotNet and JsonSchema.Net were logged `is disabled` and never looked up. husky had no update, so a second run on a scratch copy outside the repository lowered it to 0.9.0 and added a `.csproj` declaring two versions: husky went to `renovate/dotnet-local-tools`, and both `.csproj` dependencies were logged `is disabled`, proving the C-4 hold. The `github-actions` dependencies were skipped as `github-token-required`, so that run says nothing about them.

### Action versions and the post-upgrade regeneration (0075)

Designed and built 2026-10-28 for B-002, B-009, B-013, B-014 and B-018. The hand verification § 8 plans is recorded at the end of this subsection.

- **The generator carries a workflow's existing action versions forward.** Rocket.Surgery.Nuke 2.9.12's `GitHubActionsStepsAttribute.GetConfiguration` ends, whenever the workflow file already exists, with `NormalizeActionVersions`: every `uses:` the configuration holds is replaced by the version that file already names for the same action. It runs after the `Enhancements` middleware, it is not virtual, and its own documentation says it exists "to allow renovate to upgrade actions" in the YAML - the model OQ-1 rejected. Observed on 2026-10-28: with `codecov/codecov-action@v5` and `renovatebot/github-action@v46.3.7` bumped in the build source, `./build.sh --help` and `--generate-configuration GitHubActions_ci --host GitHubActions` each rewrote the workflows unchanged; with `ci.yml` and `renovate.yml` deleted first, the same run wrote each bumped version, a one-line diff per file. So a changed declaration alone regenerates nothing (C-6, B-013), and a Rocket.Surgery.Nuke update that changes a default action version would not reach a workflow either (B-014). `./build.sh Compile` keeps whatever versions the committed workflows carry.
- **Regeneration from scratch is the `GenerateWorkflows` target**, declared in [`.build/SpechtBuild.Renovate.cs`](../../.build/SpechtBuild.Renovate.cs) with no dependencies. For each `[GitHubActionsSteps]` attribute on `SpechtBuild` it deletes the attribute's `ConfigurationFile` and starts the build assembly (`BuildAssemblyFile`) with `--generate-configuration <Id> --host <HostName>`, asserting a zero exit code - the invocation NUKE's own `InvokeBuildServerConfigurationGenerationAttribute` uses for AutoGenerate. With no file present `NormalizeActionVersions` is skipped, so every `uses:` is the build's: the literal for an action the build project declares (C-6), the generator's default for one the generator emits. The set of workflows is read from the attributes, so a sixth workflow needs no edit here. Verified on 2026-10-28: with all five workflows deleted, regeneration reproduced the committed `ci.yml`, `main.yml`, `mirror.yml`, `release.yml` and `renovate.yml` byte for byte, so the committed workflows are already the from-scratch generation and the first update pull request carries only its own change. A normal build afterwards normalizes against those files and changes nothing. A person applying a declaration by hand runs the same target. The target joins `.nuke/build.schema.json`, regenerated in the same change; no workflow invokes it, and the generator emits steps only for a workflow's invoked targets, so no generated workflow changes for it.
- **Rejected for the regeneration.** Two post-upgrade commands, `rm` of the five files and `./build.sh --help` to trigger AutoGenerate: Renovate 44 runs a post-upgrade command without a shell (`allowShellExecutorForPostUpgradeCommands` defaults to `false`; the command is split with `shlex`), so the file list would be a hand copy of the attributes, and `--help` as a generation trigger is a side effect. A subclass of the attribute: `NormalizeActionVersions` is non-virtual and called from inside `GetConfiguration`. Letting the `github-actions` manager edit the YAML, as the library intends: C-3 and C-6.
- **The custom manager** (C-6, B-002) is one `customManagers` entry in [`.github/renovate.json`](../renovate.json): `customType: "regex"`; `managerFilePatterns: ["/^\\.build/[^/]+\\.cs$/"]`; `matchStrings: ["Uses = \"(?<depName>[\\w.-]+/[\\w.-]+)@(?<currentValue>[^\"]+)\""]`; `datasourceTemplate: "github-tags"`; `versioningTemplate: "github-actions"`; `depTypeTemplate: "action"`; and a `description` citing C-6. Renovate names it `custom.regex` in `matchManagers`. Today it captures five declarations: `renovatebot/github-action@v46.3.7` in `SpechtBuild.Renovate.cs`, and `docker/login-action@v3`, `azure/login@v2`, `codecov/codecov-action@v5` and `actions/upload-artifact@v7` in `SpechtBuild.GitHubActions.cs`. `github-actions` is the versioning Renovate 44's own `github-actions` manager gives an action: a floating major tag such as `v5` is a range, so it is offered only a new major, and a full tag such as `v46.3.7` is offered minor and patch releases. The manager reads the build source and nothing under `.github/workflows/`.
- **B-002's Given cannot occur in today's tree; the gap is recorded, not closed.** Of the five declarations only `renovatebot/github-action@v46.3.7` is a full tag. `docker/login-action@v3`, `azure/login@v2`, `codecov/codecov-action@v5` and `actions/upload-artifact@v7` are floating major tags, offered only a new major, so no two declarations can have minor or patch updates at once and the `renovate/github-actions` group stays empty until two declarations are full tags. They stay floating by [decision 0002](decisions/0002-floating-major-action-tags-stay-floating.md) (owner, 2026-10-28): a floating tag already takes the action author's minor and patch releases on every run with no pull request, and pinning would move each of them to a pull request and change the `uses:` lines CI runs, for no behaviour a claim asks for. B-002's grouping therefore applies to full-tag declarations only. The rule is in place, so a declaration written with a full tag joins the group with no configuration change. `docker/login-action` and `azure/login` are `DeployMiddleware`'s and generate nothing ("Not changed by 0075" below).
- **One pull request for action minor and patch updates** (B-002): a `packageRules` entry with `matchManagers: ["custom.regex"]`, `matchFileNames: [".build/*.cs"]`, `matchUpdateTypes: ["minor", "patch"]` and `groupName: "GitHub Actions"`, branch `renovate/github-actions`. An action major is not grouped; whether it waits for a person is 0076's (B-007, B-012).
- **No manager reads a generated workflow** (C-3, B-009): `"github-actions": {"enabled": false}` replaces today's `"enabled": true`. Every file under `.github/workflows/` is generated and the repository has no `action.yml`, so the manager has nothing else to read; overriding its `managerFilePatterns` cannot do the same, because a manager's patterns add to its defaults. No `customManagers` pattern and no `matchFileNames` names a path under `.github/workflows/`. The only place a workflow path appears is the post-upgrade `fileFilters` below, which chooses what the regeneration commits and matches no dependency, so a workflow changes in an update pull request only as the target's output.
- **The post-upgrade regeneration** (B-013, B-014, C-7) is two `packageRules` entries carrying the same `postUpgradeTasks`: `commands: ["./build.sh GenerateWorkflows"]` and `fileFilters: [".github/workflows/*.yml"]`.
  - Actions: `matchManagers: ["custom.regex"]` and `matchFileNames: [".build/*.cs"]`.
  - NUKE: `matchManagers: ["nuget"]`, `matchFileNames: ["Directory.Packages.props"]` and `matchPackageNames: ["Nuke.Common", "Rocket.Surgery.Nuke"]`. "The NUKE package" of B-014 and C-7 is both. Rocket.Surgery.Nuke is the generator - the `[GitHubActionsSteps]` attribute, the step types and the default action versions - and Nuke.Common carries NUKE's configuration generation and its writer; either can change a generated workflow, which is C-7's test. The other `Nuke.*` packages reach the build only through Nuke.Common, so no update of theirs is proposed on its own.
  - Neither rule sets `matchUpdateTypes`: C-7 regenerates for every update that can change a generated workflow, and a major changes one as readily as a minor.
  - `executionMode` stays at its default, `update`: the task runs for each matching upgrade, after every file update of the branch is written. `branch` would read the branch's merged configuration, which in a group comes from its first upgrade, so a NUKE package that is not first in the "NuGet packages" group would be skipped. The target is idempotent; running it twice costs only time.
  - `fileFilters` commits only the workflows. Anything else the build writes - `.nuke/build.schema.json` when a NUKE update changes it, `.nuke/temp/` - is left out of the pull request.
  - **Never on an SDK update** (the handoff in "An SDK update branch for 0075" above). Neither rule can match `global.json`'s `dotnet-sdk` dependency - the file, the manager and the package names all differ - so `renovate/net-sdk` runs no task and never starts a build that `rollForward: latestFeature` cannot satisfy. The local tool group runs none either.
  - Order: both rules, and the B-002 group, come before the C-4 hold and the engine hold, so the engine hold stays last.
- **The allowlist** (C-7, C-2) is `allowedCommands: ["^\\./build\\.sh GenerateWorkflows$"]` in [`.github/renovate-global.json`](../renovate-global.json), the name C-7 uses since its 2026-10-28 amendment. Renovate 44 still migrates the old name, `allowedPostUpgradeCommands`, but `renovate-config-validator --strict` rejects a configuration that needs migration, so the old name is never written. The command runs in the clone's root, split into `./build.sh` and its argument; `build.sh` is committed executable.
- **What the build host needs in the container.** Two facts found on 2026-10-28 go beyond the SDK B-016 installs:
  - Renovate 44 clones a GitHub repository blobless (`--filter=blob:none`; a full clone is only for Bitbucket Server). Nerdbank.GitVersioning, which `Directory.Build.props` adds to `.build` too, fails there: in a local blobless clone of this repository `dotnet build .build/.build.csproj` stopped with "An blob object with SHA … could not be found". With `NBGV_GitEngine=Disabled` it built, and a from-scratch regeneration with that variable set reproduced all five workflows. `renovate-global.json` therefore sets `customEnvVariables: {"NBGV_GitEngine": "Disabled"}`; Renovate passes a child process only a fixed list of variables plus these. The workflow generation reads no version.
  - The build host targets `net10.0` (`0001-F2` B-045), and `global.json` pins an SDK 11 whose only runtime is .NET 11. The build cannot roll forward onto it: under `DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD`, NUKE 10.1.0 throws in `NukeBuild`'s type initializer (`assemblyLocation == string.Empty || assemblyLocation == invokedLocation`) when `build.sh` starts it with `dotnet run`. So the run installs the .NET 10 SDK CI sets up as well. The literal `10.0.401` that `Middleware`, `MirrorMiddleware` and `ReleaseMiddleware`'s release job each wrote as `DotNetVersion` is now one constant, `BuildHostSdkVersion`, beside `RunnerPool` in [`SpechtBuild.GitHubActions.cs`](../../.build/SpechtBuild.GitHubActions.cs). `RenovateMiddleware` reads it too: it adds `DOTNET_BUILD_SDK_VERSION` with that value to the Renovate step's `env` and as a second line of `additional-env-list` (the action reads the input with `getMultilineInput`, one name per line). The value starts with `|`: Rocket.Surgery.Nuke's step writer emits a value starting with `|` or `>` as a YAML block scalar and quotes every other value on one line, so a bare newline would have produced a single-quoted scalar broken across lines, which a YAML parser rejects. [`.github/renovate-entrypoint.sh`](../renovate-entrypoint.sh) runs `install-tool dotnet "$DOTNET_BUILD_SDK_VERSION"` beside the existing install, before `runuser -u ubuntu renovate`. `ci.yml`, `main.yml`, `mirror.yml` and `release.yml` are unchanged by the constant.
- **`renovate.yml` is regenerated by 0075**, because `RenovateMiddleware` changes: the step gains `DOTNET_BUILD_SDK_VERSION` and `additional-env-list` becomes a block scalar of two lines. No other workflow changes, and no step moves. An SDK update still needs no regeneration.
- **Seams for § 8.** Every mechanism above is a committed file or the build's own output, readable without Renovate, a registry or the network. B-002: the `matchStrings` pattern is RE2, and its named groups read the same in .NET's `Regex`, so it can be applied to synthetic `Uses = "owner/repo@v1.2.3"` lines and to the `.build/*.cs` sources, whose captures are the build project's declared actions; the group rule's matchers and `groupName` are literal settings. B-009: `github-actions.enabled` is `false`, and no manager pattern or `matchFileNames` entry matches a path under `.github/workflows/`. B-013 and B-014: each rule's `postUpgradeTasks.commands` entry matches an `allowedCommands` pattern in `renovate-global.json`, `fileFilters` names only `.github/workflows/*.yml`, and no rule carrying `postUpgradeTasks` matches `global.json` or the `dotnet-sdk` type. That the committed workflows are the from-scratch generation is the target's output, compared with the committed files; the generated `renovate.yml`'s `additional-env-list` splits into both names on a newline. What only a live run shows: containerbase installing both SDKs where one `dotnet` sees both runtimes, the build compiling in Renovate's own clone, and a pull request carrying the regenerated workflows.
- **Not changed by 0075.** `DeployMiddleware` in `SpechtBuild.GitHubActions.cs` is referenced by no attribute, so its `docker/login-action` and `azure/login` declarations generate nothing; the custom manager still proposes their updates, as pull requests that change the build source and regenerate no workflow. The actions the generator emits - `actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/setup-dotnet@v4`, `actions/upload-artifact@v4`, `actions/download-artifact@v4` - are declared by no source in this repository and move only with a Rocket.Surgery.Nuke update (B-014).
- **Verified by hand when 0075 was built**, 2026-10-28, locally and with nothing sent to GitHub: no token, no non-dry Renovate run, no push. The plan is § 8's.
  - **Validation.** `renovate-config-validator --strict` from Renovate 44.155.1 accepted `renovate-global.json` as global configuration and `renovate.json` with `--no-global` as repository configuration, each "Config validated successfully". The local copy has no `re2` module, so it checked the regular expressions with JavaScript's `RegExp` and said so.
  - **Extraction.** A `--platform=local --dry-run=lookup` run of Renovate 44.155.1 with no token and `LOG_LEVEL=debug` logged `github-actions is disabled` and matched the ten `.build/*.cs` files for the custom manager. It extracted exactly the five declarations, as `action` dependencies with `github-tags` and `github-actions` versioning: `renovatebot/github-action` `v46.3.7` from `SpechtBuild.Renovate.cs`, and `docker/login-action` `v3`, `azure/login` `v2`, `codecov/codecov-action` `v5` and `actions/upload-artifact` `v7` from `SpechtBuild.GitHubActions.cs`. Every lookup was skipped as `github-token-required`, so the run shows extraction and the disabled manager, not the `renovate/github-actions` grouping. No dependency came from a file under `.github/workflows/`; the path appears only in the configuration's `fileFilters`. Nuke.Common 10.1.0 and Rocket.Surgery.Nuke 2.9.12 were extracted from `Directory.Packages.props` with no update available, so no rule carrying the task had anything to match. The run exited `1` only because Renovate 44.155.1 logs an unsupported Node.js 24.4.0 as an error.
  - **Regeneration from scratch.** `./build.sh GenerateWorkflows` deleted and regenerated all five workflows. `git diff -- .github/workflows` showed only the intended `renovate.yml` change, the `DOTNET_BUILD_SDK_VERSION` env line and the two-line `additional-env-list`; `ci.yml`, `main.yml`, `mirror.yml` and `release.yml` came back byte for byte. A YAML parser read `additional-env-list` as `DOTNET_SDK_VERSION` and `DOTNET_BUILD_SDK_VERSION`, one per line, and every job's step order is unchanged. A second run of the target, and `./build.sh Compile` after it, left the same diff.
  - **A bumped declaration.** With `codecov/codecov-action@v5` changed to `@v6` in `SpechtBuild.GitHubActions.cs`, `./build.sh Compile` changed no workflow. `./build.sh GenerateWorkflows` then changed one line in `ci.yml` and one in `main.yml`, each `uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5` to `@v6`, and nothing else. After the edit was reverted by hand, the target restored both files.
  - **The blobless clone** (B-018). The branch tip was cloned with `--filter=blob:none` into the repository's ignored `.artifacts/`, not outside the repository, because this session could not write there; serving the filter needed `--upload-pack` with `uploadpack.allowFilter`. `remote.origin.partialclonefilter` read `blob:none` and `git rev-list --missing=print` listed 3,906 missing blobs. 0075's change is uncommitted, so it was applied to that clone's working tree as a patch, which leaves the history NBGV walks unchanged. Without `NBGV_GitEngine`, `./build.sh GenerateWorkflows` failed while compiling `.build` with "An blob object with SHA … could not be found". With `NBGV_GitEngine=Disabled` the target succeeded, and its five workflows matched the worktree's regeneration exactly.

## 8. Testing Strategy

<!-- last written by: test-writer, 2026-10-28 (0075) -->

- **The build has no tests (owner, 2026-10-08), and this workflow is the build's.** "I don't think we need ReqnRoll (or any tests) for the build. Keep what we have, in case I change my mind, don't wire them into CI." That decision is recorded in [`0055-F2` § 8](../../.build/ContinuousIntegration/.spec/README.md). `renovate.yml` is generated by the same build, from [`SpechtBuild.Renovate.cs`](../../.build/SpechtBuild.Renovate.cs), so the decision applies here unchanged. `dependency-updates.feature` is not linked into `test/acceptance`, and no step class or unit test exists for it. Every § 9 row is therefore `Missing`: nothing pins these claims, and a step class that never ran would pin nothing either.
- **The last acceptance criterion of items 0073, 0074 and 0075 is superseded.** "§ 9 carries a row naming a test for each id above" is overruled by the owner's decision: B-010, B-011, B-015 and B-016 (0073), B-001, B-003, B-004 and B-008 (0074) and B-002, B-009, B-013, B-014 and B-018 (0075) keep their § 9 rows, each `Missing`, with no test named. Each of 0075's five has its tagged scenario in `dependency-updates.feature`.
- **Mechanisms, per claim.** Read in [`SpechtBuild.Renovate.cs`](../../.build/SpechtBuild.Renovate.cs), the generated [`renovate.yml`](../workflows/renovate.yml), [`renovate.json`](../renovate.json) and [`renovate-entrypoint.sh`](../renovate-entrypoint.sh). None has a test, by the owner's decision above.
  - B-010: a literal setting. `renovate.json` sets `dependencyDashboard: false`, and no package rule sets `dependencyDashboardApproval`, so no update waits on an issue.
  - B-011: a literal setting. `renovate.json` sets `labels: ["dependencies"]`, which applies to every pull request Renovate opens.
  - B-015: literal settings in the generated workflow. The trigger is `schedule: cron: '0 10 * * 1'`, and the Renovate step's `env` sets `RENOVATE_REPOSITORIES: ${{ github.repository }}`, so the run names this repository and no other.
  - B-016: an ordering. A bash step writes `jq -r .sdk.version global.json` into `DOTNET_SDK_VERSION`, which `additional-env-list` passes into the container. The entrypoint runs `install-tool dotnet "$DOTNET_SDK_VERSION"` and only then `runuser -u ubuntu renovate`, under `set -euo pipefail`, so a failed install stops the run before Renovate starts.
  - B-001: literal settings in `renovate.json`. A `packageRules` entry matches the `nuget` manager, `matchFileNames: ["Directory.Packages.props"]` and `matchUpdateTypes: ["minor", "patch"]`, and sets `groupName: "NuGet packages"`, so every such update lands on one branch and one pull request.
  - B-003: literal settings in `renovate.json`. A rule matches the `nuget` manager's `matchDepTypes: ["dotnet-sdk"]` - the type it gives `global.json`'s `sdk.version` - for minor and patch, and sets `groupName: ".NET SDK"`, so the SDK has its own pull request.
  - B-004: literal settings in `renovate.json`. A rule matches the `nuget` manager, `matchFileNames: [".config/dotnet-tools.json"]`, minor and patch, and sets `groupName: "dotnet local tools"`. The file name is the only thing separating it from B-001's group, since both files give their packages the same `depType`.
  - B-008: an ordering of literal settings. The last rule in `packageRules` matches `matchPackageNames: ["Markdig", "YamlDotNet", "JsonSchema.Net"]` with `enabled: false`. Renovate applies every matching rule in order and a later rule's setting wins, so no earlier grouping rule, and no rule added before it, can switch an engine dependency back on. The C-4 hold before it - a `nuget` rule whose `matchFileNames` lists only negations of the three declaring files, with `enabled: false` - keeps a version declared anywhere else, such as a `.csproj`, from being updated.
  - B-005 to B-007, B-012 and B-017: not built yet (items 0076 and 0077).
- **Mechanisms for 0075's claims**, read in § 7's "Action versions and the post-upgrade regeneration (0075)", which was designed and not built when this was written. None has a test, by the owner's decision above; each has the seam § 7 names.
  - B-002: a mapping, then a grouping. The `custom.regex` manager reads only `managerFilePatterns: ["/^\\.build/[^/]+\\.cs$/"]` and maps each `Uses = "owner/repo@version"` in them to an `action` dependency, `github-tags` datasource, `github-actions` versioning. Applied to today's sources, the pattern captures the five declarations § 7 names. The versioning decides what is offered: a full tag such as `v46.3.7` gets minor and patch releases, a floating major tag such as `v5` only a new major. The group rule (`custom.regex`, `.build/*.cs`, minor and patch, `groupName: "GitHub Actions"`) puts every offered minor and patch on `renovate/github-actions`, one pull request.
  - B-009: an exclusion. `"github-actions": {"enabled": false}` stops the one manager that reads `.github/workflows/`, and no `customManagers` pattern or `matchFileNames` names a path there. The only workflow path is the post-upgrade `fileFilters`, which picks what the regeneration commits and matches no dependency. So a workflow changes only as `GenerateWorkflows` output.
  - B-013: an ordering. The actions rule (`custom.regex`, `.build/*.cs`) carries `postUpgradeTasks` with `./build.sh GenerateWorkflows`, run in `executionMode: update` after the branch's file updates are written, and allowlisted by `allowedCommands: ["^\\./build\\.sh GenerateWorkflows$"]`. The target deletes each `[GitHubActionsSteps]` attribute's `ConfigurationFile` before it starts the build assembly with `--generate-configuration <Id> --host <HostName>`, so `NormalizeActionVersions` has no file to carry versions from and the changed declaration wins. `fileFilters: [".github/workflows/*.yml"]` commits the workflows with the declaration.
  - B-014: a mapping. The NUKE rule matches `nuget`, `Directory.Packages.props` and `matchPackageNames: ["Nuke.Common", "Rocket.Surgery.Nuke"]`, with no `matchUpdateTypes`, and carries the same task. Under `executionMode: update` the task runs for the NUKE upgrade wherever it sits in the "NuGet packages" group. No rule carrying the task can match `global.json`'s `dotnet-sdk`, so `renovate/net-sdk` never runs it.
  - B-018: the environment a child process gets. `customEnvVariables: {"NBGV_GitEngine": "Disabled"}` in `renovate-global.json` lets `.build` compile in Renovate's blobless clone. One constant beside `RunnerPool` feeds `DotNetVersion` in `Middleware`, `MirrorMiddleware` and `ReleaseMiddleware` and `DOTNET_BUILD_SDK_VERSION` in `RenovateMiddleware`, which also adds it as the second line of `additional-env-list`. The entrypoint runs `install-tool dotnet "$DOTNET_BUILD_SDK_VERSION"` before `runuser -u ubuntu renovate`, under `set -euo pipefail`.
- **Verified by hand when 0073 was delivered.** `./build.sh Compile` regenerated `renovate.yml` and nothing else; `ci.yml` was unchanged. On 2026-10-09, `renovate-config-validator --strict` from `renovate@44` accepted `renovate.json` and `renovate-global.json`. `Format` and `Test` passed. These checks show the configuration is valid. They do not show a run's behaviour.
- **Verified by hand when 0074 was delivered.** `renovate-config-validator --strict` at Renovate 44 accepted both JSON files again, and two local `--platform=local --dry-run=lookup` runs of Renovate 44 against real registries, recorded in § 7, showed the grouping and the holds as claimed: the NuGet packages and the SDK each on their own branch (B-001, B-003), husky alone on `renovate/dotnet-local-tools` on a scratch copy (B-004), the engine's three logged `is disabled` and never looked up (B-008), and a `.csproj` version held (C-4). A dry run opens no pull request, so these show the branches Renovate would create, not the pull requests GitHub would show.
- **Verified by hand when 0075 is delivered.** This is the plan; each result goes into § 7's 0075 subsection when it is run. No step uses a token or a credential.
  - **Validation.** `renovate-config-validator --strict` from `renovate@44` accepts `renovate.json` and `renovate-global.json`, as global and as repository configuration. `--strict` fails on a configuration that needs migration, so it rejects `allowedPostUpgradeCommands` where `allowedCommands` is meant (C-7).
  - **Extraction.** A local `--platform=local --dry-run=lookup` run of Renovate 44 against the tree, with no token and `LOG_LEVEL=debug`, logs `custom.regex` extracting the five `.build/*.cs` declarations as `action` dependencies (B-002) and extracts nothing under `.github/workflows/` (B-009). Without a token the `github-tags` lookups may be skipped as `github-token-required`, as 0074's were. If so, the run shows extraction and the disabled manager, not the `renovate/github-actions` grouping, and the record says so. A lookup dry run stops before any branch is written, so it runs no post-upgrade task.
  - **Regeneration from scratch.** `./build.sh GenerateWorkflows` on the delivered tree leaves `git diff --exit-code -- .github/workflows` clean: all five workflows regenerate byte for byte, and `renovate.yml` carries both `additional-env-list` names, one per line (B-013, B-018). A `./build.sh Compile` after it changes no workflow.
  - **A bumped declaration.** Change one declaration in `.build`, such as `codecov/codecov-action@v5` to `@v6`. `./build.sh Compile` alone changes no workflow (lesson 0015). `./build.sh GenerateWorkflows` then changes exactly the `uses:` lines naming that action, in each workflow that uses it, and no other line (B-009, B-013). Revert the edit by hand, not with `git checkout`, because 0075's work is uncommitted. Then rerun the target and confirm the workflows match their state before the bump.
  - **The blobless clone** (B-018). Clone a commit that carries 0075's change with `--filter=blob:none` into a scratch directory outside the repository. Confirm `git config remote.origin.partialclonefilter` reads `blob:none`, because a filter the source refuses is ignored without an error and the clone is then a full one. In that clone, `dotnet build .build/.build.csproj` without `NBGV_GitEngine` fails with the blob-not-found error. With `NBGV_GitEngine=Disabled`, `./build.sh GenerateWorkflows` completes and the five workflows match the committed ones.
- **What only a live run shows, for 0075.** All of it waits on the `RENOVATE_TOKEN` secret (item 0091).
  - B-018: containerbase installing both SDKs, one `dotnet` seeing both, and the build compiling in Renovate's own clone with only the variables Renovate passes a child process.
  - B-013 and B-014: Renovate running the allowlisted command without a shell and committing only `.github/workflows/*.yml`.
  - B-009: a live action pull request's workflows match what `./build.sh GenerateWorkflows` writes when rerun on its branch. `renovate/net-sdk` runs no task.
  - B-002: needs two declarations with full tags and minor or patch releases. Today only `renovatebot/github-action@v46.3.7` has a full tag, and the four floating major tags are offered only majors (0076's), so this tree cannot meet B-002's Given yet.
  - B-014: only after Nuke.Common or Rocket.Surgery.Nuke publishes a release.
- **Nothing has been observed live.** The first live observation is a `workflow_dispatch` run after the merge, once the owner creates the `RENOVATE_TOKEN` secret (decision 0001). That run should show `install-tool dotnet` completing before Renovate's first log line (B-016), and should open no issue (B-010). B-011's label is observable only on the first pull request Renovate opens, and B-015 only on the first scheduled Monday run. For 0074's claims, the first run with updates available should open at most one pull request each from `renovate/nuget-packages` (B-001), `renovate/net-sdk` (B-003) and `renovate/dotnet-local-tools` (B-004), and none touching Markdig, YamlDotNet or JsonSchema.Net (B-008); B-004 is observable only once a local tool has a minor or patch release.
- **Verdict.** B-001, B-003, B-004, B-010, B-011 and B-015 are literal settings with no logic of their own; a test would assert configuration, not behaviour. B-008's hold depends on rule order, which a dry run against a fixture tree could pin, but only through Renovate itself and its registries, which a test may not reach. B-016's ordering lives in a shell script inside the Renovate container, and only a run shows it. The generated step list is testable as it stands, given `RenovateMiddleware`'s output, as `0055-F2`'s rewrite is. No claim has a test because the owner decided the build needs none, not because the design prevents it.
- **Verdict for 0075.** The mechanisms are a mapping (B-002, B-014), an exclusion (B-009), an ordering (B-013) and a child environment (B-018), and each has the seam § 7 names. The match pattern can run over synthetic `Uses =` lines and the `.build/*.cs` sources. Each task command must match an `allowedCommands` pattern. No rule carrying the task may match `global.json` or `dotnet-sdk`. The target's output can be compared with the committed workflows. No claim has a test, by the owner's decision. Hard to test, reported to implementer:
  - `GenerateWorkflows` deletes files and then builds a `--generate-configuration` argument for a process it starts, all inside a target body. Pinning the argument or the delete-before-generate order needs that step taken out of the target.
  - `executionMode`, regex matching in `allowedCommands` and how `customEnvVariables` reaches a child process are Renovate's behaviour. A test reaches them only through Renovate.
  - B-002's Given cannot occur in today's tree (above).

## 10. Lessons / Spec Deltas

<!-- last written by: spec-author, 2026-10-09, 2026-10-23 (`0055-F2` decision 0005), 2026-10-28 (0075, decision 0002) -->

- 2026-10-28, decision 0002 (the owner, asked directly): the floating major action tags stay floating, so B-002's grouping applies to full-tag declarations, today only `renovatebot/github-action@v46.3.7`. § 5 row 8 added; no claim changes.

- 2026-10-28, item 0075's design (§ 7) found three facts the specification did not state. C-7 amended: Renovate 44 renamed `allowedPostUpgradeCommands` to `allowedCommands`, and `renovate-config-validator --strict` rejects the old name; the constraint's meaning is unchanged. B-018 added: the generation also needs the .NET 10 SDK the build host targets (`0001-F2` B-045) and must build in Renovate's blobless clone, which Nerdbank.GitVersioning cannot read; B-016 keeps its pinned-SDK claim, delivered by 0073, and B-018 claims the generation completing. Rocket.Surgery.Nuke 2.9.12 carries an existing workflow's action versions into its regeneration, so a changed declaration reaches a workflow only through `./build.sh GenerateWorkflows` ([lesson 0015](../../.spec/lessons/0015-an-action-version-change-needs-a-from-scratch-regeneration.md)); B-009, B-013 and B-014 are unchanged.

That decision does not apply to the Renovate workflow: it stays on GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest`, as decision 0001 and A-2 state, which the owner did not overturn (`0055-F2` C-12, § 5 #29). No claim, constraint or scenario of this Feature changes.

- 2026-10-08, C-1, § 1 and § 5 row 3 amended, following `0001-F1` decision 0004 (the owner): no baseline tag is placed, so the exclusion holds until `0001-F1` B-004's golden baseline test is on `main`, not until a tag exists. The B-008 scenario's precondition follows.

- 2026-10-09, decision 0001 (the owner, while item 0073 was planned): the Renovate workflow can also be started by hand, which is not claimed (§ 5 row 6); C-8 names its token secret `RENOVATE_TOKEN`; A-2 states that the run uses GitHub's hosted runner, not a self-hosted one (§ 5 row 7). No claim changes.
